kill_fact: The adverse case is marked below the observed arms-length price of the very assets it stresses, and it uses a balance sheet that has since been superseded. The record values the Calpine gas and geothermal fleet at $20.4B in the adverse case, about $729 per kilowatt across roughly 28 gigawatts, on compressed spark spreads. On 6 August 2026 Constellation agreed to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center to LS Power for $860M, about $1,420 per kilowatt, and disclosed that the full set of divestitures required by the Department of Justice should raise about $5.9B gross, roughly $1,200 per kilowatt, against the roughly $960 per kilowatt implied by what it paid for the Calpine assets. The finance chief made the point explicitly that this price was struck in spite of recent weakness in the Texas market - that is, inside the soft-power world the adverse case assumes. Marking the fleet at the lowest of those primary comparables, the $960 per kilowatt Constellation itself paid, adds $6.5B to adverse-case enterprise value. After also moving net debt to the $23.623B carried on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, from the $21.30B March figure the record used, the adverse case moves from $180 to $194 a share. That is a repricing, not a kill: against a live price of $277.64 the ground to the downside is still roughly three and a half times the ground to fair value, so the record's finding - poor risk and reward at today's price, wait for a lower entry - survives intact and is if anything reinforced, because the price has risen since the record was written.
corrections: Four corrections, three of which moved a load-bearing number. First, net debt. The record uses $21.30B from the 31 March 2026 balance sheet. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet, filed 6 August 2026, carries total debt of $24.700B against cash of $1.077B, so net debt is $23.623B - $2.32B higher, largely because roughly $2.2B was spent on share repurchases. This flows through every scenario and is the one correction that works against the name. Second, the share count. The record divides by 359.1 million shares; the second-quarter filing reports 354.0 million weighted-average diluted shares. I have used 354.0 million, which is deliberately conservative, since shares actually outstanding at the end of the period are lower again after the buybacks. Third, the adverse-case gas mark, described in the kill fact: $20.4B re-marked to $26.9B on primary transaction evidence. Fourth, and this one is a change of fact rather than of arithmetic, the record's own confirming conditions for the bear case have largely resolved against it, two days after the record's as-of date. The record named four: a second-quarter miss or guidance trim on 6 August; another quarter with no large contract signed; PJM or the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission landing large-load rules that shift value to consumers; and free cash flow running near $1B annualised rather than tracking toward $4.2B. On 6 August adjusted operating earnings came in at $2.55 a share against a $2.36 consensus, up about 33% on the year, and full-year guidance was raised by $0.50 to $11.50-$12.50 - the opposite of a miss or a trim. Roughly 920 megawatts of long-term nuclear contracts were disclosed as signed since the prior call, averaging 18.5 years with investment-grade customers, taking contracted clean baseload output to about 30% - so the 'nothing signed' condition has failed, and the catalyst status of SOFT_EXTENDED is now stale, though the single very large transaction the market has been waiting on remains unannounced and 920 megawatts is not that deal. On regulation the movement was toward the company, not away: the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ordered every regional operator to justify its large-load interconnection tariffs and pressed PJM on co-location, pulling expected rule clarity forward to the first or second quarter of 2027 from PJM's earlier 2029 target. The fourth condition, however, verifies and has got worse, and this is the part of the bear case that stands up: free cash flow over the twelve months to 30 June 2026 was $309M - operating cash flow of $4.206B less capital spending of $3.897B - down from the $1.14B the record cites, against a guided run-rate of roughly $4.2B a year. Capital spending is still climbing. Cash conversion remains the honest hole in this name and the number to re-check every quarter. Two further notes that carry no numeric correction: the administrative ceiling on the PJM capacity market is unchanged and the record's reading of it stands, and the record's caution on returns on invested capital is untested until the combined company has reported more quarters.

corrections_typed.basis: Adverse-case gas and geothermal mark of $20.4B (~$729/kW on ~28GW) sits below arms-length comps struck inside the adverse case's own soft-power scenario: 6 Aug 2026 agreement to sell Brazos Valley Energy Center to LS Power for $860M (~$1,420/kW), with total Department of Justice mandated divestitures disclosed at ~$5.9B gross (~$1,200/kW) versus ~$960/kW implied Calpine purchase price. Re-marked at the lowest comp, $960/kW x 28GW = $26.9B, +$6.5B, lifting adverse enterprise value from $85.9B to $92.4B. Less net debt of $23.623B (30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, filed 6 Aug 2026: total debt $24.700B less cash $1.077B) = $68.78B over 354.0M Q2 weighted-average diluted shares = $194.

Same enterprise value of $129.0B on the record's own schedule, less updated net debt of $23.623B (30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, filed 6 Aug 2026) rather than the $21.30B at 31 Mar 2026, = $105.38B over 354.0M Q2 weighted-average diluted shares = $298. The base-case gas mark of $30.0B (~$1,071/kW) already sits inside the observed $960-$1,420/kW transaction range and is left unchanged.

Same enterprise value of $157.7B on the record's own schedule, less updated net debt of $23.623B (30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, filed 6 Aug 2026) rather than $21.30B at 31 Mar 2026, = $134.08B over 354.0M Q2 weighted-average diluted shares = $379.

evidence: Constellation Energy second-quarter 2026 results and Form 10-Q, filed 6 August 2026: adjusted operating earnings $2.55 per share (GAAP $1.42) against a $2.36 consensus, up about 33% year on year; full-year 2026 adjusted operating earnings guidance raised $0.50 to $11.50-$12.50 from $11.00-$12.00. Balance sheet at 30 June 2026: total debt $24.700B less cash and equivalents $1.077B = net debt $23.623B, against $22.466B and $1.171B (net $21.295B) at 31 March 2026. Weighted-average diluted shares 354.0 million.

Constellation Energy second-quarter 2026 earnings call, 6 August 2026 (Joe Dominguez, Shane Smith): approximately 920 megawatts of long-term nuclear agreements signed since the prior call, average duration 18.5 years, investment-grade customers, taking contracted clean baseload output to roughly 30%; agreement with LS Power to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center for $860 million, about $1,420 per kilowatt, achieved 'in spite of recent ERCOT weakness'; Department of Justice mandated divestitures expected to generate approximately $5.9 billion gross at nearly $1,200 per kilowatt against an implied $960 per kilowatt purchase price for the Calpine assets; approximately $2.2 billion of share repurchases deployed since the end of March with $2.8 billion of authorisation remaining.

Constellation Energy trailing-twelve-month cash flow to 30 June 2026 (Form 10-Q filed 6 August 2026): net cash from operating activities $4.206B less capital expenditure $3.897B = free cash flow $309M, down from the $1.14B the record cites and far below the guided run-rate of roughly $4.2B a year. The record's cash-conversion objection verifies and has deteriorated.

Constellation Energy second-quarter 2026 earnings call, 6 August 2026, on regulation: the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ordered every regional transmission organisation to justify how existing tariffs provide for interconnection of large loads and directed PJM to explain why co-located transmission services cannot be made available more quickly; management now expects co-location rule clarity in the first to second quarter of 2027 against PJM's earlier 2029 target, with PJM's reliability backstop procurement targeted at 6.8 gigawatts and an auction this autumn with results by year-end. The record's condition that PJM or the Commission would land rules shifting value to consumers has not materialised to date. Live price $277.64 (NASDAQ, 11 August 2026) against the $268.73 used in the record.

Constellation Energy Corporation press release, 4 August 2026: quarterly dividend of $0.4265 per share declared, payable 4 September 2026 to holders of record 18 August 2026 - unchanged, confirming the record's reading that there is no income-holder washout in prospect.
